purpose: How a GPS/fleet-tracking reseller reasons about which fleets to target and why they buy, chooses between platform-reseller and white-label economics, builds honest per-unit economics from real vendor quotes, designs the hardware-plus-subscription offer, and sells on ROI grounded strictly in the customer's own numbers inside lawful-tracking and disclosure boundaries.
assumptions: no observed dataset supplied; all scores are heuristic priors
the operator is a small independent reseller-installer serving a local or regional market, selling tracker hardware plus a monthly per-unit tracking-platform subscription
both channel structures (authorized platform reseller and white-label platform licensing) are available to the operator and can be quoted from real vendor agreements
every monetary quantity in this KB is a mechanism or qualitative band to be verified against the operator's own vendor quotes and the customer's own records; nothing here is a market figure
employer duties to disclose employee tracking exist as an obligation class in most jurisdictions; the exact rules are jurisdiction- and fleet-type-specific and must be verified locally
exclusions: device selection (OBD, hardwired, battery asset trackers), installation method, concealment-versus-serviceability trade-offs, platform account setup, geofence/alert/report configuration, driver-disclosure onboarding execution, and per-unit verification testing - the installation and onboarding KB owns these

per-unit MRR management, device-health and data-quality monitoring, renewal and contract hygiene on live accounts, in-account expansion (more vehicles, assets, dashcams, maintenance modules), fleet churn signals, and support economics at unit scale - the subscription and account-growth KB owns these
covert tracking of private individuals or any vehicle or asset the buyer does not own or control as an employer - such requests are refused, not serviced
asserting jurisdiction-specific ELD/hours-of-service or telematics-privacy rules as fact - this KB names obligation classes only and flags them for verification in the operating jurisdiction
invented per-unit prices, commissions, margins, savings percentages, payback periods, or market-size figures stated as fact - only mechanisms and qualitative bands, verified per deal
personalized financial, legal, tax, or insurance advice to any specific customer or to the operator

competency_questions.question: Which fleet segments should a local tracking reseller target first, and what loss or efficiency pain does each segment actually feel?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: FLEET_SEGMENT_MAP distinguishes trades, delivery, trucking, and equipment-rental segments with decision-maker and sales-cycle character, and LOSS_EFFICIENCY_PAIN_DIAGNOSIS ties each segment to its evidenced pain taxonomy

competency_questions.question: Where does a tracking reseller's money actually come from on one tracked unit, and what moves each revenue and cost line?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: RESELLER_MONEY_MODEL_FRAME names the revenue lines (hardware, install, monthly subscription) and PER_UNIT_ECONOMICS_MODEL decomposes the per-unit cost stack and its sensitivities as mechanisms built from the operator's own quotes

competency_questions.question: Should the operator run as an authorized platform reseller or license a white-label platform, and what evidence justifies switching later?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: PLATFORM_RESELLER_MECHANICS and WHITE_LABEL_MECHANICS each describe who owns brand, billing, support, and account book, and CHANNEL_MODEL_DECISION states the volume, capability, and book-ownership conditions under which each wins

competency_questions.question: How is the hardware-plus-subscription offer packaged and priced - upfront hardware versus subsidized hardware inside a term, and what belongs in the monthly line?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: HARDWARE_MARGIN_SOURCING explains the two hardware postures as mechanisms, OFFER_ARCHITECTURE sets the packaging choices, and PRICING_TERM_STRUCTURE ties price floors and term length to hardware recovery

competency_questions.question: How does the reseller build an ROI case a fleet owner believes without inventing a single savings figure?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: CUSTOMER_NUMBERS_ROI_CASE requires the customer's own fuel, payroll, loss, and dispute records as the only inputs with conservative ranges, and ETHICAL_SELLING_RULES bans invented savings percentages outright

competency_questions.question: Which tracking requests must be refused outright, and what disclosure commitment is a precondition of every employer sale?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: LAWFUL_TRACKING_BOUNDARY restricts service to owner/employer-authorized vehicles and assets with required employee disclosure and names private-individual covert requests as refusals with a scripted decline

competency_questions.question: When does a prospect's ask cross into regulated territory such as ELD/hours-of-service or telematics privacy, and what does the reseller do at that line?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: REGULATED_CLASS_FLAG_MAP names the obligation classes, the fleet types that trigger them, and the verify-or-refer action instead of asserting jurisdiction-specific rules

competency_questions.question: What events open a fleet's buying window, and how does the reseller sell into a theft or dispute incident without fear-selling?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: DEMAND_TRIGGER_WATCH lists the trigger events and their outreach timing, and ETHICAL_SELLING_RULES limits incident selling to the customer's own facts and figures

competency_questions.question: How does the operator size the serviceable local fleet market and turn it into a named prospect list without inventing a market-size figure?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: LOCAL_MARKET_SIZING_LIST_BUILD counts observable fleets from public and street-level evidence and produces a named, segmented list with unit-count bands rather than a claimed total-market number

competency_questions.question: How does a local reseller win against national self-serve telematics platforms and cheap consumer DIY trackers?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: COMPETITIVE_WEDGE_POSITIONING states the install-configure-service wedge, where each competitor genuinely wins, and the price-floor discipline that keeps the wedge profitable

competency_questions.question: How is the equipment and asset-owner niche commercially different from vehicle fleets for a tracking reseller?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: EQUIPMENT_ASSET_NICHE distinguishes theft-recovery and utilization pain, battery-tracker economics with sparser reporting, insurance-driven demand, and renter-disclosure questions from the vehicle-fleet pattern

competency_questions.question: How is a paid pilot structured so its results convert into a fleet-wide rollout instead of an argument?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: PILOT_PROOF_DESIGN requires a written baseline, agreed success criteria drawn from the diagnosed pain, a bounded unit subset and duration, and a pre-agreed rollout decision rule

competency_questions.question: Who are the people inside a fleet deal, and how do driver concerns and internal politics shape whether it closes?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: BUYER_ROLES_AND_DRIVER_PUSHBACK separates owner, fleet manager, dispatcher, and bookkeeper roles by what each fears and gains, and treats driver pushback as a deal risk addressed by disclosure framing, not concealment

competency_questions.question: What must be true about a deal before it hands off to installation and platform onboarding?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: QUALIFIED_HANDOFF_GATE lists the pass conditions - lawful-use check, disclosure commitment, signed decision-maker, unit list with use cases, ROI case on the customer's numbers, agreed price and term, regulated-class flags resolved - and holds failures with the failed condition named

glossary.definition: One vehicle or asset carrying an active tracker and platform subscription; the base unit of recurring revenue, cost, and account size in every reseller calculation.

A channel structure where the reseller sells and installs hardware under the platform vendor's brand and the vendor operates the platform; the reseller earns hardware/install margin plus a recurring share or wholesale-retail spread defined by the dealer agreement - the agreement, not a universal rate, sets the number.

A channel structure where the operator licenses the tracking platform under their own brand, pays the vendor a per-unit platform fee plus data/SIM cost, sets retail pricing, and owns billing, first-line support, and the customer relationship end to end.

The full recurring cost behind one tracked unit - platform fee, cellular data/SIM, financed hardware amortization, and a support-time allowance - assembled from the operator's actual vendor quotes; the stack's total defines the price floor.

Discounting or zero-pricing the tracker upfront and recovering its cost inside the monthly subscription across a committed term; the mechanism trades upfront margin for recurring volume and only works when the term guarantees recovery.
The minimum monthly per-unit price at which every line of the per-unit cost stack is covered with a stated buffer; discounting below it turns each new unit into a recurring loss.

A savings model whose only inputs are the customer's own records - fuel bills, payroll and overtime, theft or loss history, disputed invoices - presented as conservative ranges, never as invented industry savings percentages.

A time-bounded state of purchase readiness opened by an event - a theft, an insurance premium review, a billing dispute, fleet growth - during which a fleet that previously ignored tracking will take a meeting.

The family of rules requiring certain commercial fleets to log driving hours electronically; which fleets are covered and what devices qualify is jurisdiction- and fleet-type-specific, so the reseller flags it for verification rather than asserting coverage.

The employer's act of informing employees that work vehicles are tracked, an obligation class in most jurisdictions and a hard precondition of sale in this KB; the reseller sells disclosed tracking or does not sell.

source_registry.description: heuristic prior estimates for fleet_tracking_market_and_reseller_economics work units in absence of supplied datasets
source_registry.citation_or_locator: heuristic prior; no external dataset supplied

nodes.definition: Fix the money model before anything else: a tracking reseller earns on three lines per tracked unit - a one-time hardware sale (or financed hardware), one-time install labor, and a monthly platform subscription that repeats for the life of the unit - and the business's value concentrates in the recurring line because it compounds with every unit while hardware margin is earned once. The frame names each line's mechanism: hardware margin comes from the spread between distributor cost and sale price, install margin from labor priced per vehicle class, and subscription margin from the spread between what the platform vendor charges the reseller (or shares with them) and what the fleet pays. Every downstream choice - segment, channel, offer, price - is judged by what it does to durable per-unit spread, not to this month's hardware invoice.

included: the three revenue lines and their margin mechanisms
the tracked unit as the base of account math
excluded: actual dollar figures for any line
install labor technique
live-account MRR management

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: a signed vendor agreement restates which party bills the fleet or how recurring margin is shared

pros.claim: Naming the recurring line as the business's center of gravity stops the operator optimizing for hardware invoices that never repeat
pros.example: choosing a slightly lower hardware markup to win a 30-van fleet whose subscriptions repeat monthly for years

cons.claim: Recurring-first framing can starve near-term cash that a new operator needs to survive
cons.example: a first-year reseller subsidizing hardware on every deal and running out of cash before subscription volume covers overhead

failure_modes: treating the business as a hardware shop and pricing subscriptions as an afterthought
quoting deals with no idea which line carries the margin, so discounts land on the only profitable line
acceptance_tests: the operator can state, for any quoted deal, which of the three lines carries margin, by what mechanism, and what a discount on each line does to per-unit spread
revisit_triggers: the platform vendor changes how the recurring line is shared or billed
the operator's mix shifts materially between hardware-led and subscription-led deals

nodes.definition: Draw the bright line every deal must sit inside: the reseller tracks only vehicles and assets the buyer owns or controls as an employer, and every employer sale carries a disclosure commitment - employees are told their work vehicles are tracked before units go live. Requests to track a spouse, an ex-partner, a private individual's car, or any vehicle the requester does not own are refused with a short scripted decline, no referral to a workaround, regardless of deal size. The boundary is commercial as well as legal: a reseller known for covert work loses fleet accounts that need defensible tracking, and a single covert job can implicate the operator in stalking or harassment exposure. This node owns the refusal script, the ownership/authority check performed on every prospect, and the disclosure commitment captured in writing before handoff.

included: employee-disclosure commitment as a sale precondition
scripted refusal of private-individual and covert requests
excluded: executing driver-disclosure onboarding sessions
jurisdiction-specific statute citations, which are flagged for verification not asserted

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: a refused-request pattern, enforcement action, or updated legal guidance changes the authority check or the refusal script

pros.claim: A hard refusal line protects the operator from the highest-severity legal and reputational exposure in the tracking trade
pros.example: declining a walk-in asking to slip a tracker onto a partner's car, and logging the refusal, instead of booking easy hardware margin

cons.claim: The boundary costs real revenue from gray-zone requests that a looser competitor will take
cons.example: losing a small-fleet owner who wants trackers kept secret from drivers and buys from an online shop instead

failure_modes: accepting an employer's claim of authority without checking the vehicles are actually company-owned or company-controlled
closing a fleet deal while quietly letting the owner skip employee disclosure to avoid friction
acceptance_tests: every open deal has a recorded ownership/authority check and a written disclosure commitment, and every declined covert request is logged with the refusal script used
no quote exists for a private individual's vehicle or an undisclosed employee-tracking arrangement
revisit_triggers: a prospect pattern emerges that the current refusal script handles badly
legal guidance or a local enforcement action redraws where the authority line sits

nodes.definition: Map the regulated territory the reseller must recognize but never freelance: ELD/hours-of-service mandates apply to certain commercial fleets (typically weight-, distance-, and cargo-dependent) and only certified devices satisfy them; telematics-privacy and employee-monitoring rules govern what may be collected about drivers and how it is disclosed; and some fleet types (passenger transport, hazmat, cross-border) carry extra obligation classes. The reseller's competence is naming the class a prospect's ask falls into and firing the verify-or-refer action - check current rules in the operating jurisdiction, or refer to a compliance specialist or the platform vendor's certified offering - rather than asserting whether this fleet is covered. Selling a plain tracking package while implying it satisfies an ELD mandate is the canonical error this node exists to prevent.

included: obligation-class recognition (ELD/HOS, telematics privacy, employee monitoring, special fleet types)
the verify-or-refer action at the regulated line
keeping compliance claims out of unverified quotes
excluded: asserting which specific fleets are covered in any jurisdiction
operating or configuring certified ELD products, which belongs to installation and onboarding

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: a regulatory change notice, vendor certification change, or misplaced fleet type shows the class map is stale

pros.claim: Class-plus-flag competence lets a small reseller serve regulated-adjacent fleets without pretending to be a compliance consultant
pros.example: telling an interstate hauler 'that ask falls under hours-of-service rules - we verify current requirements for your fleet type before quoting' instead of guessing

cons.claim: Flagging instead of answering slows deals and can look like ignorance next to a competitor who confidently asserts
cons.example: a rival closing a trucking deal in one visit by promising ELD coverage the reseller would have sent to verification

failure_modes: implying a non-certified tracking bundle satisfies an ELD mandate
missing that a prospect's fleet type triggers an obligation class at all, so the flag never fires
acceptance_tests: every quote touching a regulated-class fleet carries either a verification note with jurisdiction named or a referral, and no quote asserts compliance coverage the operator has not verified
revisit_triggers: a jurisdiction updates ELD, hours-of-service, or employee-monitoring rules
a prospect fleet type appears that the current class map does not place

nodes.definition: Segment the addressable fleets by how they buy, not just what they drive: trades and field service (plumbers, electricians, HVAC - owner-led, 3 to 30 vans, buys on billing disputes and side-job suspicion, short sales cycle); local delivery and courier (route-driven, buys on fuel and route efficiency, dispatcher influence strong); trucking and haulage (heavier compliance surface, longer cycles, may already run telematics and be switching); and equipment rental and construction (asset theft and utilization pain, buys around insurance events). Each segment entry records typical fleet-size band, who signs, the dominant pain, the sales-cycle shape, and how defensible the reseller's wedge is there. The map picks a beachhead segment for repeatable install and offer patterns instead of chasing every fleet type at once.

included: segment definitions with buyer, pain, cycle, and size band
excluded: individual prospect qualification
device choice per segment, which belongs to installation

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: closed-won/closed-lost patterns or local fleet composition shifts contradict the segment entries

pros.claim: A buying-character map lets one small operator build repeatable offers instead of bespoke pitches per fleet
pros.example: standardizing a trades-fleet package after three near-identical HVAC deals closed on the same billing-dispute pain

cons.claim: Early segment commitment can lock the operator onto a beachhead the local market cannot feed
cons.example: picking long-haul trucking in a county whose carriers all run national platform contracts already

failure_modes: pitching every segment with the same generic 'know where your vehicles are' story
choosing a beachhead by personal familiarity rather than evidenced local density and pain
acceptance_tests: each segment entry names its decision-maker, dominant pain, cycle shape, and size band, and one beachhead is chosen with a stated local-evidence reason
revisit_triggers: win-rate or cycle-length evidence contradicts a segment entry
a new segment (e.g. municipal or agricultural fleets) appears in the local market

nodes.definition: Diagnose, with the customer's own records, which of the recurring fleet pains tracking genuinely addresses: vehicle and equipment theft or unauthorized after-hours use; fuel burned in idling and off-route miles; unverifiable timesheets and side jobs on company vehicles; customer billing disputes that die without proof of arrival and time-on-site; dispatch inefficiency from not knowing who is closest; and missed maintenance from untracked mileage. For each pain the node specifies what evidence to ask for (fuel bills, disputed invoices, overtime records, a theft report, insurance correspondence) and what tracking can and cannot do about it - a tracker locates a stolen van but does not prevent the break-in; it evidences idling but does not by itself change driver behavior. Diagnosis output is a ranked pain list per prospect with the record that proves each, which becomes the raw material of the ROI case.

included: the pain taxonomy and its evidence sources
what tracking does and does not fix per pain
excluded: quantifying savings, which the ROI case owns
configuring alerts or reports against a pain, which belongs to onboarding

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: pilot measurements or account outcomes contradict the diagnosed pain ranking for a segment

pros.claim: Evidence-first diagnosis turns the pitch from product features into the prospect's own operating problem
pros.example: opening a second meeting with the prospect's three disputed invoices on the table instead of a tracker spec sheet

cons.claim: Asking for internal records early feels intrusive to owners who have not yet decided to trust the reseller
cons.example: a plumbing-fleet owner refusing to share payroll data with a vendor he met last week, stalling diagnosis

failure_modes: asserting a pain the customer has not confirmed and building the whole offer on it
promising behavior change (less idling, no side jobs) that only management action, not the tracker, can deliver
acceptance_tests: each qualified prospect has a ranked pain list where every entry cites a customer-provided record or a customer-confirmed statement, not an assumed industry problem
revisit_triggers: pilot or account evidence shows a diagnosed pain was misranked
a segment's dominant pain shifts (e.g. fuel prices fall and idling drops down the ranking)

nodes.definition: Treat equipment and asset owners - construction contractors, tool-and-plant rental yards, trailer and container fleets - as a commercially distinct niche rather than a small vehicle fleet. The pain profile is theft recovery and utilization, not driver behavior: a stolen compressor or skid steer is a five-figure loss with an insurance dimension, and rental yards additionally want to bill utilization and find equipment their customers moved. The economics differ mechanically: battery-powered asset trackers report position a few times a day instead of every few seconds, which means lower data cost per unit, longer service intervals, and often a lower monthly price line but a much higher unit count per account (every trailer, every generator). Demand frequently arrives insurance-driven - after a theft claim or a premium negotiation where the insurer asks what anti-theft measures exist. Renter-facing disclosure questions (tracking equipment while customers rent it) get flagged to the regulated-class map rather than answered from instinct.

excluded: battery-tracker model selection and mounting, which belongs to installation
asserting insurance-premium effects as fact

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: vendor asset-tracker economics or local insurer anti-theft recognition changes

pros.claim: Asset accounts multiply unit count per customer far beyond their vehicle fleets
pros.example: a rental yard with six vans but ninety taggable assets - trailers, breakers, towers - each carrying a subscription line

cons.claim: Sparse-reporting trackers disappoint buyers who expected live vehicle-style tracking on assets
cons.example: a contractor angry that his stolen generator's tracker last reported four hours before the theft window

failure_modes: quoting asset units at vehicle-tracker data assumptions and wrecking the per-unit stack
promising theft 'prevention' when the mechanism is after-the-fact location and recovery support
acceptance_tests: asset-niche quotes use the sparse-reporting cost mechanics and state recovery-support (not prevention) as the theft value, and renter-disclosure questions carry a verification flag
revisit_triggers: an insurer in the local market changes what anti-theft measures it recognizes
asset-tracker reporting economics shift (battery life, data pricing) at the vendor

nodes.definition: Map the humans in a fleet deal because tracking touches everyone who drives: the owner (or GM) signs and cares about loss and margin; the fleet or ops manager runs the system daily and becomes either champion or saboteur; the dispatcher gains the most usable value (nearest-vehicle routing) and is a natural internal advocate; the bookkeeper feels billing disputes and overtime leakage and can substantiate the ROI case from records. Drivers are not buyers but can kill deals: tracking reads as accusation, and organized or informal pushback ('we'll quit', devices unplugged) has ended rollouts. The reseller's posture is to surface driver reaction as a named deal risk in the sales conversation, arm the owner with disclosure-first framing (tracking protects drivers in disputes and false-claim accusations too), and never accept the shortcut of hiding devices from staff - that shortcut belongs to the refusal script.

included: driver pushback as sales-stage deal risk with disclosure-first framing
excluded: running driver-disclosure onboarding sessions, which installation-and-onboarding owns
union consultation procedure, which gets a regulated-class flag

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: lost-deal reviews attribute failures to role dynamics the current map does not capture

pros.claim: Knowing who gains what lets the reseller recruit an internal champion instead of selling alone from outside
pros.example: winning a courier fleet by giving the dispatcher a nearest-vehicle demo while the owner watched the reaction

cons.claim: Multi-role selling stretches a solo operator's time across meetings a small deal may not repay
cons.example: four meetings with owner, ops manager, and bookkeeper to close a five-van account

failure_modes: selling only to the owner and meeting the ops manager for the first time at install day as an opponent
letting the owner plan a quiet no-disclosure rollout to avoid driver friction, which violates the boundary and poisons the account
acceptance_tests: every qualified deal names the signer, the daily operator, the likely champion, and the expected driver-reaction risk with the disclosure framing to be used
revisit_triggers: a deal dies from an unmapped role or unexpected driver reaction
a segment shows a consistently different decision structure than the map assumes

nodes.definition: Catalog the events that convert an indifferent fleet into an open buying window, because tracking is rarely bought cold: a theft or break-in (the strongest single trigger), an insurance premium review or insurer questionnaire asking about anti-theft and fleet-safety measures, a painful billing dispute a customer refused to pay, a fuel-cost spike that makes idling visible on the P&L, fleet expansion past the size an owner can supervise by eye, a failed experiment with cheap consumer trackers, and a new contract (municipal, corporate) that requires vehicle tracking or proof-of-service. The watch is operational: the prospect list carries trigger-relevant notes, local theft and construction-site-crime reporting is monitored, and outreach is timed to the window with a scoped, factual message rather than year-round generic canvassing. Trigger selling stays inside the ethical rules - the window is entered with the prospect's facts, never with amplified threat statistics.

excluded: fear-based messaging, banned by the ethical rules
post-sale expansion triggers inside live accounts, which the account-growth KB owns

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: meeting-source tracking shows a trigger class has gone cold or a new event class is producing meetings

pros.claim: Trigger-timed outreach reaches fleets at the moment tracking stops being an abstract expense
pros.example: a roofing contractor who ignored two cold calls booking a meeting the week after two of his trailers vanished from a yard

cons.claim: Trigger-dependent pipelines are lumpy and can leave long quiet stretches in a small market
cons.example: a low-crime winter with stable fuel prices producing six weeks of no inbound interest

failure_modes: drifting from trigger response into ambulance-chasing that leans on fear
having no monitoring wired to the list, so windows open and close unseen
acceptance_tests: each active prospect carries its trigger state, and every window-timed outreach message references only the prospect's own event and facts
revisit_triggers: a trigger class stops producing meetings
a new trigger (new contract-award requirements, local crime pattern) appears in the market

nodes.definition: Size the serviceable market by counting observable fleets, not by quoting an industry market-size figure: enumerate local trades and field-service firms from licensing and trade-association rosters, delivery and courier operators from business directories, haulers from carrier registries where public, and rental yards and contractors from street-level and site observation - liveried vans photographed in one industrial estate are data. Each prospect enters the list with a fleet-size band estimated from evidence (vehicles seen, jobs advertised, yard size), a segment tag, and a serviceability note (drive-time from the operator's base, since install visits are physical work). The output is a named, segmented, banded list whose totals are described honestly as observed counts with an unseen tail, and which doubles as the substrate the trigger watch monitors. The channel decision consumes the total tracked-unit potential band this list implies.

included: named list with size bands and serviceability
honest observed-count framing with an unseen tail
excluded: claiming a total addressable market figure as fact
per-prospect pain diagnosis, owned by its own node

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: list-versus-field audits reveal systematic banding errors or a materially changed serviceable radius

pros.claim: A counted, named list converts market strategy from opinion into a work queue
pros.example: eighty-two named fleets within forty minutes' drive, banded by size, replacing 'there must be plenty of fleets around here'

cons.claim: Observable counting undercounts low-visibility fleets and can misjudge the beachhead's real depth
cons.example: home-based contractors whose vans sit in driveways across three towns never appearing in any roster or estate walk

failure_modes: inflating the list with out-of-range or single-vehicle entries to make the market look deep
building the list once and letting it rot instead of feeding the trigger watch
acceptance_tests: every list entry carries a segment tag, an evidence-based size band, and a serviceability note, and list totals are labeled as observed counts, not market size
revisit_triggers: field evidence shows a band or segment tag pattern is systematically wrong
the serviceable radius changes (new installer hired, base moved)

nodes.definition: Position the local reseller where national self-serve telematics platforms and cheap consumer DIY trackers structurally cannot follow: the platform giants sell online with published per-unit pricing but ship boxes for the fleet to self-install and self-configure; consumer trackers are cheap but bring no fleet platform, no install, and no accountable local human. The reseller's wedge is the bundle of physical install across mixed vehicle types, configuration mapped to the fleet's actual workflow, one accountable local person, and continuity when devices fail - and the positioning discipline is to sell that wedge explicitly rather than hiding it inside a monthly price that then looks expensive next to a self-serve headline rate. The node also owns honest concession: a tech-comfortable two-van operation may genuinely be fine self-installing a consumer device, and saying so preserves credibility for the fifteen-van deal where the wedge is real.

included: honest concession where DIY genuinely fits
excluded: pricing below the cost-stack floor to match self-serve rates
disparaging competitor claims the operator cannot evidence

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: competitor moves (local install partnerships, price restructuring) or loss reviews invalidate the wedge story

pros.claim: Selling the wedge explicitly reframes the comparison from per-unit price to delivered outcome
pros.example: quoting install, workflow configuration, and local support as named lines beside the monitoring line, so the self-serve comparison stops being like-for-like

cons.claim: The wedge story fails with buyers who only compare headline monthly prices
cons.example: a price-driven courier owner choosing a self-serve platform's online rate and churning the conversation on cost alone

failure_modes: burying install and service value inside one monthly number and losing on apparent price
overclaiming against national platforms whose product is genuinely strong, destroying trust when the buyer checks
acceptance_tests: every competitive quote itemizes the wedge (install, configuration, local service) as named value lines and contains no competitor claim the operator cannot support
revisit_triggers: a national platform adds local install partnerships in the operator's market
repeated losses show the wedge story failing in a specific segment

nodes.definition: Understand the authorized platform-reseller (dealer) structure as a mechanism before comparing it to anything: the platform vendor owns the software, the brand the fleet sees, and usually the subscription billing relationship; the reseller sells and installs hardware, brings the account, and earns hardware/install margin plus a recurring component defined entirely by the dealer agreement - a revenue share on subscriptions, a wholesale-to-retail spread, or a per-activation bounty, whichever the contract states. The mechanism's virtues are low operating burden (no billing system, no platform support desk, vendor-run infrastructure) and fast start; its structural costs are thin recurring spread, pricing set by the vendor's published rates, exposure to vendor changes in commission terms, and - decisive for exit value - the account book typically belonging contractually to the vendor, not the reseller. The node's discipline is reading the actual agreement for who bills, who owns the account on termination, and what the recurring component is, rather than assuming any industry-standard split exists.

included: dealer-structure roles (brand, billing, support, book ownership)
recurring-component forms as defined by the agreement
excluded: asserting any standard commission percentage
the white-label structure, owned by its sibling node

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: the operator's dealer agreement terms change or a rival vendor's dealer structure is quoted for comparison

pros.claim: The dealer route lets a one-person installer sell a serious fleet platform from day one with no billing or support infrastructure
pros.example: closing a 20-vehicle account in the first month because the vendor's platform, app, and support desk already exist

cons.claim: Vendor-owned billing and book mean the reseller's recurring income exists at the vendor's discretion
cons.example: a dealer agreement amendment cutting the recurring share on renewals, with the accounts contractually unmovable

failure_modes: signing a dealer agreement without establishing who owns the account book on termination
modeling the recurring component from a rumor about what other dealers earn instead of the contract text
acceptance_tests: the operator can point at the clauses in their own dealer agreement that define the recurring component, the billing party, and account-book ownership on termination
revisit_triggers: the vendor amends commission, billing, or termination terms
a competing platform offers a materially different dealer structure

nodes.definition: Understand the white-label structure as the ownership-heavy alternative: the operator licenses the tracking platform under their own brand, pays the vendor a per-unit platform fee plus SIM/data cost (the wholesale stack), sets their own retail monthly price, and owns billing, collections, first-line support, and the entire customer relationship. The spread between retail and the wholesale stack is the operator's to design - which is why white-label margins can be structurally wider than dealer shares - but everything the vendor did in the dealer model becomes the operator's job and cost: invoicing and failed payments, support tickets at 7am, churn absorption, and platform-fee exposure on units that sit unbilled. The book of accounts belongs to the operator, which is what makes a white-label base a sellable asset. The node's discipline is costing the ownership burden honestly - support time, billing tooling, bad debt - into the wholesale stack before admiring the wider spread, and reading the license terms for minimum unit commitments and fee-change rights.

included: white-label roles (own brand, own billing, own support)
book ownership and its exit value
license terms: minimum commitments, fee-change rights
excluded: asserting typical white-label fees or margins as figures
live-account support operations, which the account-growth KB owns

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: white-label license terms change or measured ownership-burden costs contradict the modeled stack

pros.claim: Owning brand, billing, and book converts subscription volume into a durable, sellable asset
pros.example: a white-label base of tracked units under the operator's own brand being valued and sold as a book, which a dealer's vendor-owned accounts cannot be

cons.claim: The ownership burden lands regardless of scale - billing, support, and bad debt cost real hours from unit one
cons.example: a two-person shop losing its install week to chasing failed card payments and a platform-outage support storm

failure_modes: admiring the retail-wholesale spread while omitting support time and bad debt from the stack
signing minimum-unit commitments sized for hoped-for growth rather than the counted local market
acceptance_tests: the operator's white-label evaluation prices the full wholesale stack including support-time and bad-debt allowances, and quotes the license's minimum-commitment and fee-change clauses
revisit_triggers: the vendor changes per-unit platform fees, data pricing, or minimum commitments
the operator's measured support cost per unit diverges from the allowance in the stack

nodes.definition: Decide the channel structure as an evidence-gated choice, not an identity: start-state favors the dealer model when the operator is new, cash-thin, and unproven at support and billing, because it converts installs into income immediately with no infrastructure; the white-label case strengthens as three evidences accumulate - a counted local market deep enough to clear the license's minimum commitments, demonstrated capacity to run billing and first-line support without cannibalizing install capacity, and enough unit volume that the designed retail-wholesale spread beats the dealer's recurring component by more than the ownership burden costs. The decision records its trigger thresholds in advance (unit count, support-hours evidence, cash reserve) so 'graduate to white-label' is a gate that fires on evidence rather than on ambition, and it prices the switching cost honestly: dealer-model accounts usually cannot be migrated, so switching mid-book means running two structures or abandoning vendor-owned accounts. Hybrid postures (dealer for one platform, white-label for assets) are legitimate outcomes.

excluded: negotiating specific vendor contracts
re-platforming live accounts operationally, which the account-growth KB touches

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: a pre-registered graduation threshold is crossed or either channel's vendor terms materially change

pros.claim: Pre-registered graduation thresholds stop the operator lurching into white-label on a good quarter's optimism
pros.example: declining a white-label license because the counted list cannot clear the minimum commitment even at full penetration

cons.claim: Deliberate channel caution can strand a capable operator on thin dealer spreads longer than necessary
cons.example: an operator with proven support capacity leaving book-ownership value unclaimed for a year of threshold-checking

failure_modes: choosing white-label for brand vanity while the unit count cannot carry the ownership burden
ignoring that existing dealer accounts cannot migrate and modeling the switch as a clean cutover
acceptance_tests: the channel choice cites the three evidences (market depth vs minimums, support capacity, spread-vs-burden comparison) and the switch thresholds are written before they are approached
revisit_triggers: a graduation threshold is crossed or a vendor materially changes either structure's terms
measured support burden or churn contradicts the spread-vs-burden comparison

nodes.definition: Manage hardware as a deliberate margin posture, not a pass-through: source trackers through the platform vendor's device catalog or approved third-party distributors (compatibility with the platform is the binding constraint), and decide per deal between two postures - sell hardware at a markup upfront, taking margin now and keeping the subscription line clean, or subsidize hardware (discounted or bundled at no upfront charge) and recover its cost inside the monthly line across a committed term. The subsidy mechanism is a loan in disguise: the tracker's landed cost plus install labor must be recoverable from the term's subscription spread with a buffer for early cancellation, or the posture is charity. Sourcing discipline covers landed cost (unit, shipping, duty), warranty terms and dead-on-arrival handling, firmware/platform compatibility, and not warehousing more stock than the pipeline justifies. No specific markup or unit price is asserted anywhere - the posture math runs on the operator's actual distributor quotes.

included: sourcing checklist: landed cost, warranty, compatibility, stock depth
excluded: device-type selection per use case (OBD vs hardwired vs battery), which installation owns
asserting device prices or markups as figures

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: distributor quotes, warranty terms, or cancellation-loss experience change the posture math

pros.claim: A deliberate per-deal posture lets hardware serve strategy - margin when cash is needed, subsidy when recurring volume is worth buying
pros.example: subsidizing trackers on a 25-van term deal to remove the upfront-cost objection, while selling hardware at full markup to a 4-van no-term buyer

cons.claim: Subsidized hardware concentrates loss on early cancellation, and stock sourcing ties up cash either way
cons.example: a subsidized 10-unit account cancelling at month five, leaving unrecovered device and install cost on units now bolted into someone else's vans

failure_modes: subsidizing hardware into no-term or weak-term deals where recovery is unenforceable
buying stock from an incompatible or gray-market source and discovering the platform will not activate the devices
acceptance_tests: every subsidized deal has a term whose subscription spread recovers landed hardware plus install cost with a stated buffer, and every stocked device model is confirmed platform-compatible in writing
revisit_triggers: distributor pricing, warranty terms, or device availability shift
early-cancellation losses show the recovery buffer is too thin

nodes.definition: Build the per-unit profit-and-loss as a living mechanism assembled only from the operator's real numbers: on the cost side, the platform fee or forgone share (per the chosen channel), cellular data/SIM cost, amortized hardware and install cost when subsidized, and a support-time allowance per unit; on the revenue side, the monthly subscription plus any amortized upfront charges. The model exposes the quantities every other decision consumes: the cost-stack price floor (the monthly price below which a unit recurs at a loss), the payback horizon on subsidized deals (months of spread needed to recover upfront cost), and sensitivity - what a data-price change, a platform-fee change, or one extra support call per month does to spread. The honesty rule is structural: the model's cells hold the operator's actual vendor quotes and measured times, and when this KB discusses the model it names the lines and the mechanism, never an invented example figure presented as typical. A deal that cannot clear the floor at its proposed price is visible before it is signed, which is the model's entire job.

included: the cost-stack lines and revenue lines per unit
price floor, payback horizon, and sensitivity outputs
excluded: asserting any typical per-unit figure
portfolio-level MRR reporting on live accounts, which the account-growth KB owns

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: a changed vendor quote, data price, platform fee, or measured support time invalidates a model line

pros.claim: A per-unit model makes bad deals visible at quote time instead of at year-end
pros.example: a requested multi-fleet discount showing up immediately as pricing twelve units below the floor before anyone signs

cons.claim: Per-unit precision can hide account-level effects like shared install trips and support batching
cons.example: declining a marginal 15-unit deal that one shared install day and pooled support would actually have made profitable

failure_modes: populating the model with remembered or rumored numbers instead of current vendor quotes
omitting the support-time allowance so every unit looks more profitable than it recurs
acceptance_tests: every model line cites its source (vendor quote, distributor invoice, measured support time) with a date, and the computed floor and payback horizon are re-derived after any input change
no quoted deal prices units below the current floor without a written exception rationale
revisit_triggers: any vendor quote, data price, or platform fee changes
measured support time per unit diverges from the modeled allowance

nodes.definition: Design the offer the fleet actually signs from the per-unit model and the diagnosed pain: choose the hardware posture (upfront purchase, subsidized-in-term, or full rental where the operator retains device ownership), define what the monthly line includes (platform access, data, support response, warranty-swap of failed devices) so value is named rather than implied, and set the tier structure - a base tracking tier and clearly-priced additions - without dragging in expansion products (dashcams, maintenance modules) that belong to later account growth. Offer design is segment-tuned: trades fleets respond to simple per-van pricing with dispute-proof reporting named in the bundle; asset owners need the sparse-reporting asset tier priced to its cheaper data reality; term length is chosen with the pricing node to protect subsidy recovery. Every packaging choice traces to a floor check in the per-unit model and to a diagnosed pain it answers - an offer element no diagnosed pain asked for is cost, not value.

excluded: in-account expansion offers (dashcams, maintenance modules) on live accounts
device-type selection mechanics, owned by installation

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: close-rate patterns, floor movements, or service-capacity limits invalidate a package element

pros.claim: Naming what the monthly line includes converts an abstract subscription into an insurable promise the buyer can compare
pros.example: a monthly line that states platform, data, next-visit device swap, and phone support, beating a cheaper line that names nothing when a device fails

cons.claim: Rich packaging multiplies variants that a small operator must then quote, install, and honor consistently
cons.example: five tier-and-posture combinations producing quoting errors and a warranty-swap promise made to one account and forgotten on another

failure_modes: packaging an element no diagnosed pain asked for and eating its cost as unvalued weight
letting the offer promise service levels (response time, swap speed) the operator's capacity cannot honor
acceptance_tests: every offer element traces to a diagnosed pain or a named service promise, every posture-tier combination passes the per-unit floor check, and the offer sheet fits on one page a fleet owner can retell
revisit_triggers: quote-to-close data shows a tier or posture confusing buyers or losing consistently
the per-unit model's floor moves under an existing package

nodes.definition: Set price and term as mechanisms anchored to the cost stack and the subsidy math, never to a guessed market rate: the monthly per-unit price starts from the floor the per-unit model computes, adds the wedge premium the positioning node justifies (install, configuration, local service named as value), and is sanity-checked against what the fleet already pays per vehicle for comparable line items (insurance, fuel card fees) as a framing device using the customer's own bills - not as an invented benchmark. Term length is the subsidy-recovery instrument: subsidized hardware demands a term that recovers landed cost with buffer, while upfront-hardware deals can run month-to-month or short terms as a trust posture. Multi-unit discount discipline is codified in advance - volume steps, the absolute floor no discount crosses, and what is traded for a discount (longer term, full-fleet commitment, reference rights) - so negotiation never invents prices deal-by-deal. Auto-renewal, price-change notice, and early-termination mechanics are set here as offer terms; their live-account enforcement belongs to the account-growth KB.

included: pre-codified volume-discount ladder and absolute floor
renewal and termination terms as offer design
excluded: invented market-rate benchmarks
renewal execution and contract hygiene on live accounts, which the account-growth KB owns

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: cost-stack movement under the ladder or systematic won/lost pricing evidence in a segment

pros.claim: A pre-codified discount ladder with an absolute floor lets the operator negotiate fast without ever quoting a loss-making unit
pros.example: answering a 40-unit discount demand in one meeting from the ladder - deeper step in exchange for a full-fleet term - instead of improvising a price

cons.claim: Floor-anchored pricing can leave value uncaptured on fleets that would have paid substantially more
cons.example: a dispute-plagued contractor who would have paid a premium for proof-of-service reporting getting the standard ladder price

failure_modes: discounting below the floor under end-of-quarter pressure and locking a recurring loss into a multi-year term
attaching a long term to upfront-hardware deals that need no recovery protection, creating resentment without economic purpose
acceptance_tests: every quoted price decomposes into floor plus named wedge premium, every subsidized deal's term passes the recovery check, and no signed discount sits below the absolute floor
revisit_triggers: the floor moves (cost-stack change) under the published ladder
won/lost pricing evidence shows the ladder consistently mispositioned in a segment

nodes.definition: Build the ROI case exclusively from numbers the customer hands over or confirms: their fuel spend from their fuel-card statements, their disputed or written-off invoices from their books, their overtime and timesheet costs from payroll, their theft and loss history from claims and police reports, their insurance premiums from their renewal letters. The mechanism per line is stated conservatively - idling and off-route reduction is modeled as a range on their fuel figure with the honest caveat that the tracker evidences waste but management action removes it; dispute recovery is modeled on their actual disputed-invoice history, since proof-of-service reporting converts some fraction of those from write-off to paid; theft exposure uses their loss history, and any insurance-premium effect is a question for their insurer, never a promise. The output artifact is a one-page case where every input cell names its customer-provided source, ranges are wide and conservative, and the summary states what the case does not claim. A prospect who will not share records gets a pilot proposal with baseline measurement instead of a case built on invented numbers.

included: conservative range modeling per pain line
excluded: industry-average savings percentages presented as this customer's outcome
insurance-premium promises, which only the customer's insurer can make

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: measured pilot or account outcomes contradict the modeled ranges, or a source-record class becomes unavailable

pros.claim: A case made of the customer's own numbers survives the skeptical bookkeeper who kills vendor-math proposals
pros.example: the fleet's bookkeeper re-adding the disputed-invoice line from her own ledger and becoming the deal's internal advocate

cons.claim: Conservative customer-numbers cases read smaller than competitors' glossy savings claims
cons.example: losing a head-to-head to a rival deck promising a large fleet-cost reduction figure the operator refused to match

failure_modes: quietly substituting an industry savings percentage where the customer had no records
presenting the top of a modeled range as the expected outcome in the meeting even though the page says otherwise
acceptance_tests: every input cell in the ROI case names a customer-provided document or confirmed statement as its source, and the case contains no external benchmark presented as this customer's expected saving
prospects without shareable records receive a baseline-measured pilot proposal, not an estimated case
revisit_triggers: pilot or account measurements contradict a modeled range
a pain line's mechanism changes (e.g. fuel prices move enough to re-rank the case)

nodes.definition: Codify the selling rules as hard constraints, not tone suggestions: disclosure-first means the employee-disclosure requirement is raised by the reseller in the sales conversation - before the buyer asks - and a buyer who wants it skipped is declined; no-fear-selling means theft and liability are discussed only through the prospect's own incidents and figures, never through amplified crime statistics, staged urgency, or 'your fleet is being watched by thieves' theater; no-invented-numbers means every savings claim traces to the customer's records or a measured pilot; and buyer care means small owner-operators, buyers under incident stress, and buyers with limited language or financial sophistication get slower pacing, plain-language terms, explicit totals over the term, and an unpressured decision window rather than a close-now push. The rules exist because trust is the reseller's only durable moat against bigger, cheaper competitors - and because tracking, sold fearfully or opaquely, damages the very workplaces it enters. Violations are treated like safety incidents: logged, reviewed, and corrected in the scripts.

included: disclosure-first raising of employee notice in-sale
invented-number ban in all sales artifacts
excluded: the lawful/covert refusal line itself, owned by the boundary node
post-sale account communications, owned by the account-growth KB

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: a logged violation, buyer complaint, or new sales channel shows the rules are not holding in practice

pros.claim: Raising disclosure before the buyer asks converts a legal obligation into a visible trust signal
pros.example: an owner deciding on the spot because the reseller opened with how drivers are told and protected, unlike the previous vendor who whispered

cons.claim: Hard ethical constraints concede short-term wins to competitors who sell fear and inflated savings
cons.example: a rival closing an incident-shaken prospect the same afternoon with crime-wave statistics the reseller refused to use

failure_modes: urgency framing drifting from the prospect's incident into borrowed crime statistics under quota pressure
rushing an overwhelmed small buyer through term commitments they did not understand, then losing them and their referrals at renewal
acceptance_tests: every sales artifact and script passes the checks: disclosure raised proactively, urgency references only the prospect's own events, every number traces to customer records or measured data, and term totals are stated in plain language
logged violations exist as reviewed incidents with script corrections, not as unexamined wins
revisit_triggers: a violation log entry or complaint reveals a script or incentive drifting from the rules
a new sales channel (phone, web, subcontracted sales) needs the rules re-encoded

nodes.definition: Structure the pilot as a designed experiment that converts into rollout by its own terms: a bounded subset of units (enough vehicles to represent the fleet's duty cycles, few enough to bound cost), a fixed duration long enough to cover normal operating variation, a written baseline captured before install (current fuel figures, disputed-invoice run rate, timesheet pattern - drawn from the ROI case's source records), success criteria agreed in writing against the diagnosed pains (what measured change on which line counts as success), and a pre-agreed decision rule: if criteria are met, rollout proceeds at the quoted fleet-wide terms; if not, both sides walk with defined unit disposition. Pilots are paid - free pilots attract unserious buyers and devalue the wedge - though pilot fees may credit against rollout. The pilot's measured lines feed back into the ROI case as observed data replacing estimated ranges, which is the single strongest honesty upgrade available to the operator's sales material for that account and segment.

included: agreed success criteria and rollout decision rule
excluded: pilot-unit installation and configuration work, owned by installation
guaranteeing pilot outcomes in advance

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: pilot conversion rates or criterion ambiguity patterns show the pilot template needs redesign

pros.claim: A pre-agreed decision rule converts pilot success into rollout without a second sales campaign
pros.example: a 5-van pilot rolling straight into the 28-van fleet because the disputed-invoice criterion was met and the rollout terms were already signed

cons.claim: Short pilots measure noise on low-frequency pains, and theft may simply not occur during the window
cons.example: a pilot showing zero theft events and modest idle change, read by the buyer as 'tracking does nothing'

failure_modes: starting installs before the baseline is written, leaving nothing to measure change against
letting success criteria stay verbal, so pilot results become an argument instead of a decision
acceptance_tests: every pilot has a written baseline, written success criteria tied to diagnosed pains, a fixed duration, and a signed rollout decision rule before the first unit is installed
revisit_triggers: pilot results repeatedly ambiguous on a criterion class (e.g. theft) indicating criteria design must change
pilot-to-rollout conversion drops in a segment

nodes.definition: Gate every deal before it crosses into installation and onboarding with an explicit definition-of-done: the ownership/authority check is recorded and the lawful boundary holds; the employer's written disclosure commitment exists; any regulated-class flags (ELD/HOS, telematics privacy, union consultation, renter disclosure) are resolved by verification or referral, not by silence; the signer is confirmed and the internal champion named; the unit list exists with per-unit use cases (which vehicles, which assets, what each is tracked for) so installation can plan device and placement work; the ROI case or pilot result on file uses only customer numbers; and price, term, hardware posture, and discount all sit inside the codified structures with the floor respected. Deals failing any condition are held with the failed condition named and an owner assigned - never passed forward on momentum, because installation rework and post-install disputes cost multiples of a delayed signature. The gate record is the handoff artifact the installation KB receives.

excluded: installation scheduling and execution
post-install account management

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: installation rework reports or gate-hold patterns show the pass-condition checklist is wrong or incomplete

pros.claim: A hard gate stops half-qualified deals from becoming installation rework and early-life churn
pros.example: holding a signed deal because the disclosure commitment was missing, and surfacing that the owner had planned a covert rollout after all

cons.claim: Gate friction on hot deals irritates buyers and salespeople and invites quiet bypassing
cons.example: an eager 30-van buyer cooling during a week of unit-list and disclosure paperwork the gate refused to waive

failure_modes: waiving conditions for large or urgent deals, exactly the deals where failure costs most
passing a deal with an ambiguous unit list, so installation discovers unknown vehicle types on site
acceptance_tests: a deal advances only when every pass condition is checked and recorded, and every held deal names its failed condition and an owner for resolution
the handoff record contains the unit list with use cases, the disclosure commitment, resolved flags, and the signed commercial terms
revisit_triggers: installation reports rework traceable to a gate condition that passed wrongly or is missing from the checklist
gate-hold patterns show a condition is systematically failing upstream

edges.why_related: the lawful boundary scopes which revenue the money model is allowed to pursue at all
segments are ranked by what they contribute to durable per-unit spread, the frame's core quantity
the dealer structure is one concrete arrangement of the frame's three revenue lines
the white-label structure is the alternative arrangement of the same revenue lines with ownership shifted to the operator
hardware posture decisions trade the frame's one-time line against its recurring line
the regulated-class map extends the lawful boundary into jurisdiction-specific obligation territory that gets flagged, not asserted
the selling rules operationalize the boundary's disclosure requirement inside the sales conversation
pain diagnosis starts from each segment's dominant pain profile in the map
the asset niche is a segment entry deep enough to need its own economics treatment
who signs and who resists varies by segment, so the role map is segment-indexed
the list is counted and tagged against the segment definitions
trigger events are the moments a diagnosed pain becomes acute enough to open a window
the ROI case quantifies exactly the pains diagnosis ranked, using the records diagnosis identified
the decision compares the dealer structure's actual agreement terms against the alternative
the decision weighs the white-label spread against its honestly-costed ownership burden
landed hardware cost and the chosen posture are cost-stack lines in the per-unit model
under the dealer structure the model's recurring line is whatever the agreement's share mechanism yields
under white-label the model's cost stack is the wholesale platform fee, data, and ownership-burden allowances
every packaging choice must pass the model's floor check before it is offered
price and term are set on the packaging the offer defines, posture by posture
the model's computed floor and payback horizon anchor the price ladder and term rules
pilot baselines and success criteria are drawn from the ROI case's source records and modeled lines
the pilot runs on a bounded slice of the actual offer so its result prices the rollout
a pilot's decision rule outcome is one of the gate's accepted proofs of a qualified deal
the gate verifies the signed price, term, and discount sit inside the codified structures
the gate's disclosure and honest-numbers conditions are the selling rules made checkable
unresolved regulated-class flags are a gate-blocking condition before installation
the invented-number ban constrains the ROI case to customer records and conservative ranges only
no trigger event, however lucrative the window, converts a covert or private-individual request into a deal
no offer may claim ELD/HOS or privacy-compliance coverage that has not been verified for the jurisdiction and fleet type
taking hardware margin upfront and subsidizing hardware to win subscription volume pull the same offer in opposite directions
edges.resolution_rule: the per-unit model decides, not the pitch: subsidize only when the signed term's subscription spread recovers landed hardware plus install cost with the stated buffer; otherwise hardware is sold upfront at markup

edges.why_related: pressure to match a self-serve platform's headline per-unit rate collides with pricing the install-configure-service wedge
edges.resolution_rule: never price below the cost-stack floor to match a headline rate; compete by unbundling - meet the comparison on the monitoring line if needed while billing install, configuration, and service as named lines

edges.why_related: a fresh theft incident is the strongest closing window and simultaneously the highest fear-selling temptation
edges.resolution_rule: the ethical rules win: sell into the window using only the prospect's own incident and figures, no borrowed crime statistics or staged urgency, and the incident-stressed buyer gets the same plain-language terms and decision room as any other

edges.why_related: trigger events cause pilot willingness - a fleet burned by an incident funds a scoped pilot it would have refused cold
measured pilot lines flow back into the ROI case, replacing estimated ranges with observed data
deals repeatedly dying at the same gate condition re-rank segments and can move the beachhead
both structures price the same underlying objects - device, data, platform seat - and differ in who owns brand, billing, book, and risk
the named list is built first; the trigger watch then runs over exactly that list

conflict_axes.name: upfront_hardware_margin_vs_mrr_growth
conflict_axes.description: Selling hardware at full markup banks cash now; subsidizing it buys recurring volume but concentrates loss on early cancellation.
poles: subsidize hardware to grow recurring units
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: let the per-unit model choose per deal: subsidy only where the term's spread recovers landed cost with buffer, upfront margin everywhere else

conflict_axes.name: dealer_simplicity_vs_white_label_ownership
conflict_axes.description: The dealer model starts fast with no infrastructure but thin, vendor-controlled spread; white-label owns brand, billing, and a sellable book but carries the whole operating burden.
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: default to dealer while unproven; graduate on pre-registered evidence thresholds (market depth vs minimums, support capacity, spread-vs-burden), accepting that dealer accounts rarely migrate

conflict_axes.name: incident_urgency_vs_no_fear_selling
conflict_axes.description: A prospect's fresh theft or dispute maximizes closing odds exactly when fear-amplification is most tempting and most damaging.
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: sell into the window with the prospect's own facts and figures only; the stressed buyer gets standard pacing and plain-language terms

conflict_axes.name: roi_persuasion_vs_numbers_honesty
conflict_axes.description: Glossy industry savings percentages persuade faster than conservative ranges built on the customer's own records.
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: customer numbers always win; where records are missing, offer a baseline-measured pilot instead of an estimated case

conflict_axes.name: price_match_vs_service_wedge_premium
conflict_axes.description: Matching national self-serve headline rates wins comparisons but erases the margin that pays for install, configuration, and local service.
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: never breach the cost-stack floor; unbundle so the monitoring line compares while install and service are named, billed value

conflict_axes.name: segment_breadth_vs_beachhead_focus
conflict_axes.description: Serving every fleet type that calls fills the calendar; a beachhead makes offers and installs repeatable but says no to real revenue.
poles: focus the beachhead until it is repeatable
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: hold the beachhead for offer and process repeatability, taking off-segment deals only when they clear the floor without bespoke packaging work

conflict_axes.name: owner_visibility_vs_driver_acceptance
conflict_axes.description: The owner buys total visibility over vehicles and hours; drivers experience the same feature set as accusation, and their resistance can kill or hollow out the rollout.
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: sell disclosed tracking framed as protecting drivers in disputes too; surface driver reaction as a named deal risk and never resolve it by concealment

conflict_axes.name: pilot_rigor_vs_deal_momentum
conflict_axes.description: A baselined, criteria-gated pilot protects both sides but adds weeks while a hot buyer wants fleet-wide installs now.
poles: ride the momentum to a full close
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: momentum may skip the pilot only when the buyer signs fleet-wide at codified terms with the ROI case on their own numbers; it never skips the handoff gate

conflict_axes.name: compliance_upsell_vs_regulated_scope_creep
conflict_axes.description: Prospects asking for ELD or compliance coverage offer extra revenue that drags the reseller into regulated territory it cannot assert.
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: serve regulated asks only through verification or referral to certified offerings; no quote asserts compliance coverage the operator has not verified

conflict_axes.name: term_length_protection_vs_customer_trust
conflict_axes.description: Long terms protect subsidy recovery and revenue predictability but read as lock-in, breeding resentment and renewal-time revenge.
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: attach term length to its economic purpose only - subsidized hardware gets recovery terms, upfront-hardware deals earn flexible terms - and state term totals in plain language

edge_cases.description: A walk-in asks for a tracker on a spouse's or ex-partner's personal car
edge_cases.trigger: a tracking request targets a private individual's vehicle the requester does not own or control as an employer
edge_cases.mitigation: refuse with the scripted decline, no workaround referral, and log the refusal; no quote is created regardless of offered payment

edge_cases.description: A fleet owner wants devices installed without telling drivers 'so they act natural'
edge_cases.trigger: an employer buyer asks to skip or delay employee disclosure
edge_cases.mitigation: make the written disclosure commitment a non-waivable condition of sale, offer the protects-drivers-too framing, and walk away if the buyer insists on concealment

edge_cases.description: An interstate hauler asks whether the tracking package satisfies the ELD mandate for his trucks
edge_cases.trigger: a prospect's ask lands in the ELD/hours-of-service obligation class
edge_cases.mitigation: name the obligation class, state that coverage is jurisdiction- and fleet-type-specific, and verify current rules or refer to the vendor's certified ELD offering before anything is quoted

edge_cases.description: A two-van operation's own numbers show tracking cannot pay back at any honest price
edge_cases.trigger: the customer-numbers ROI case comes out negative for a small prospect
edge_cases.mitigation: say so, right-size to a minimal theft-recovery-only configuration if the prospect still wants it for peace of mind, and decline to manufacture savings that make the case pretend to work

edge_cases.description: A prospect whose van was stolen last week wants to sign anything, immediately
edge_cases.trigger: an incident-stressed buyer enters the funnel inside a fresh theft window
edge_cases.mitigation: serve the urgency with fast scheduling, not fear amplification: quote from the codified ladder, state term totals plainly, and give the standard decision room despite the buyer's rush

edge_cases.description: A fleet manager demands a guaranteed savings percentage written into the contract
edge_cases.trigger: the buyer conditions signature on a promised savings figure
edge_cases.mitigation: refuse invented guarantees; counter with a baselined pilot whose measured lines and pre-agreed decision rule give the buyer real protection instead of a fabricated number

edge_cases.description: A national platform's self-serve web price undercuts the reseller's quoted monthly line
edge_cases.trigger: the buyer produces a cheaper headline per-unit rate from a direct-selling platform
edge_cases.mitigation: unbundle the quote so monitoring compares like-for-like while install, configuration, and local service stand as named lines; concede the deal if the buyer genuinely needs none of the wedge

edge_cases.description: The white-label vendor announces a per-unit platform-fee increase affecting the whole base
edge_cases.trigger: a wholesale-stack input rises under existing customer terms
edge_cases.mitigation: re-run the per-unit model, identify units pushed under the floor, and use the offer's price-change notice mechanics on renewal rather than absorbing a recurring loss silently

edge_cases.description: A rental yard wants trackers on equipment its customers rent and take away
edge_cases.trigger: tracked assets are used by renters who are not the owner's employees
edge_cases.mitigation: treat renter notice as a flagged obligation question - rental-contract disclosure language verified for the jurisdiction - before installs are scheduled

edge_cases.description: A prospect waves a cheap consumer tracker and asks why the reseller costs more
edge_cases.trigger: the buyer benchmarks against DIY consumer hardware with no fleet platform behind it
edge_cases.mitigation: explain the platform, install, and accountable-service difference honestly, and concede the single-asset hobby case where the consumer device genuinely serves the need

edge_cases.description: A pilot ends with no theft events and only modest idle reduction on its measured lines
edge_cases.trigger: low-frequency pains produce statistically empty pilot windows
edge_cases.mitigation: read the result against the pre-agreed criteria only - dispute-proof reporting and measured idle lines - and never claim the absent theft as prevented; redesign criteria classes that cannot resolve in a pilot window

edge_cases.description: A unionized fleet's rollout requires formal employee-representative consultation before monitoring changes
edge_cases.trigger: a prospect's workforce has collective-representation consultation rights over monitoring
edge_cases.mitigation: flag the consultation obligation class for verification, keep the deal held at the gate until the employer completes its process, and support the owner with the protects-drivers-too material

workflow.description: Name the three revenue lines, their margin mechanisms, and recurring-line primacy
workflow.gate: each line's margin mechanism is stated and the recurring line's primacy is explicit

workflow.description: Write the authority check, the disclosure precondition, and the covert-request refusal script
workflow.gate: the ownership/authority check, written disclosure commitment, and scripted refusal all exist

workflow.description: List the obligation classes, the fleet types that trigger them, and the verify-or-refer action
workflow.gate: every class carries a trigger description and a verify-or-refer action; no class asserts jurisdiction specifics

workflow.action: Map fleet segments and choose the beachhead
workflow.description: Profile trades, delivery, trucking, and equipment segments by buyer, pain, cycle, and size band
workflow.gate: each segment names decision-maker, dominant pain, cycle shape, and size band; the beachhead has a local-evidence reason

workflow.action: Count the serviceable market and build the list
workflow.description: Enumerate named fleets from rosters, directories, and street observation with size bands and serviceability
workflow.gate: every entry has a segment tag, evidence-based size band, and serviceability note; totals are labeled observed counts

workflow.description: Define the pain taxonomy, the evidence to request per pain, and what tracking honestly fixes
workflow.artifact: diagnosis question set and evidence checklist
workflow.gate: each pain names its evidence source and its honest can/cannot statement

workflow.description: Compare the actual dealer and white-label terms against market depth and capacity evidence
workflow.artifact: channel decision memo with pre-registered graduation thresholds
workflow.gate: the choice cites agreement terms, market depth versus minimums, and support-capacity evidence; switch thresholds are written

workflow.description: Populate the cost stack and revenue lines from current vendor quotes and measured times
workflow.artifact: per-unit model with floor, payback, and sensitivities
workflow.gate: every line cites a dated source; floor and payback recompute after any input change

workflow.action: Design the offer architecture and pricing
workflow.description: Package hardware posture, monthly-line inclusions, and tiers; set the ladder, floors, and term rules with pricing
workflow.artifact: offer sheet plus codified price ladder and term rules
workflow.gate: every element traces to a diagnosed pain or named service promise and passes the floor check; the discount ladder and absolute floor are codified

workflow.description: Create the one-page case format whose every input cell names a customer-provided source
workflow.gate: the template admits no input without a customer source and contains the does-not-claim summary block

workflow.description: Fix subset sizing, duration, written baseline, success criteria, and the rollout decision rule
workflow.gate: baseline, criteria, duration, and decision rule are all written fields signed before any install

workflow.description: Codify the pass conditions and the hold-with-named-failure procedure feeding installation
workflow.artifact: handoff gate checklist and record format
workflow.gate: all pass conditions are checkable, holds name their failed condition and owner, and the handoff record carries the unit list, disclosure commitment, resolved flags, and signed terms
