priority_rationale: The frame nodes come first because the money model, the lawful boundary, and the regulated-class map define what the business is and what it may sell; market nodes (segments, pain, niche, roles, triggers, list, positioning) must exist before economics because channel and pricing choices consume market-depth evidence; the two channel mechanics feed the channel decision and the per-unit model, which gates all offer and pricing design; and selling nodes (ROI case, ethical rules, pilot) converge on the qualified-handoff gate, which is last because it composes every upstream obligation into the record installation receives.

dominance_rules.rule: The lawful-tracking boundary dominates every revenue opportunity
dominance_rules.rationale: one covert job creates legal and reputational exposure no deal size repays
dominance_rules.trigger: any request touches a private individual's vehicle or undisclosed employee tracking
dominance_rules.action: refuse with the script, log the refusal, create no quote

dominance_rules.rationale: an undisclosed rollout violates the boundary, poisons the account, and voids the trust moat
dominance_rules.trigger: a buyer asks to skip, soften, or delay employee disclosure
dominance_rules.action: hold the deal until the written disclosure commitment exists; walk away if refused

dominance_rules.rule: The customer's own numbers dominate any persuasive borrowed figure
dominance_rules.rationale: invented savings are the trade's signature dishonesty and unravel at the first bookkeeper audit
dominance_rules.trigger: a savings claim is drafted for any sales artifact
dominance_rules.action: trace it to a customer record or measured pilot line, or delete it and offer a baselined pilot

dominance_rules.rule: The regulated-class flag dominates deal scope
dominance_rules.rationale: asserting unverified ELD/HOS or privacy coverage converts a sales error into a compliance incident for the customer
dominance_rules.trigger: a prospect ask lands in any mapped obligation class
dominance_rules.action: verify current rules for the jurisdiction and fleet type or refer to a certified offering before quoting

dominance_rules.rule: The cost-stack floor dominates competitive price pressure
dominance_rules.rationale: a unit priced below the floor recurs as a loss for the life of its term
dominance_rules.trigger: a discount request or competitor rate would set any unit below the floor
dominance_rules.action: hold the floor, trade term or scope instead of price, and let the deal go if it cannot clear

dominance_rules.rule: Subsidy-recovery term coverage dominates discount-and-term generosity
dominance_rules.rationale: subsidized hardware without a recovering term converts every early cancellation into unrecovered cost bolted into someone else's vehicles
dominance_rules.trigger: a subsidized-hardware deal is negotiated on term length or early-exit rights
dominance_rules.action: require the term (or exit fees) to recover landed hardware plus install with buffer, or switch the deal to upfront hardware

dominance_rules.rule: Diagnosed, evidenced pain dominates product enthusiasm
dominance_rules.rationale: offers built on assumed pain produce unvalued features and churn-prone accounts
dominance_rules.trigger: an offer or proposal is drafted before the prospect's pain list exists
dominance_rules.action: stop and complete diagnosis with customer records or confirmations first

dominance_rules.rule: Walking away dominates forcing a case that cannot pay back
dominance_rules.rationale: a customer whose own numbers show no payback becomes a churning, referral-destroying account
dominance_rules.trigger: the honest ROI case comes out negative at any compliant price
dominance_rules.action: say so, right-size to the minimal honest configuration or decline, and keep the relationship for when their fleet grows

dominance_rules.rationale: guarantees on invented figures are fear's mirror image - dishonest optimism with contractual teeth
dominance_rules.trigger: a buyer conditions signature on a promised savings number
dominance_rules.action: offer the baselined pilot with its pre-agreed decision rule as the only guarantee the operator can honestly sign

anti_rework_rules.rule: Write the lawful-use policy and refusal script before the first sales conversation
anti_rework_rules.prevents: improvised answers to covert requests that entangle the operator in deals that must later be unwound and disclosed

anti_rework_rules.rule: Read both channel structures' actual agreements before signing either
anti_rework_rules.prevents: discovering book-ownership and fee-change clauses after accounts exist, when re-platforming means abandoning them

anti_rework_rules.rule: Build the per-unit cost stack from current dated quotes before publishing any price
anti_rework_rules.prevents: repricing the whole offer sheet and renegotiating live quotes after discovering units were priced under water

anti_rework_rules.rule: Diagnose pain from customer records before drafting any proposal
anti_rework_rules.prevents: rebuilding proposals around the real pain after the first meeting exposes the assumed one as wrong

anti_rework_rules.rule: Resolve regulated-class flags before scoping or quoting the deal
anti_rework_rules.prevents: retracting compliance implications from a signed quote, which converts a sale into a liability conversation

anti_rework_rules.rule: Sign the pilot's baseline, criteria, and decision rule before the first pilot install
anti_rework_rules.prevents: disputed pilot readings that stall the rollout and force a second full sales campaign

anti_rework_rules.rule: Confirm the signer and capture the unit list with use cases before ROI modeling
anti_rework_rules.prevents: modeling and presenting to someone who cannot sign, then remodeling when the real signer surfaces with different vehicles

anti_rework_rules.rule: Codify the discount ladder and absolute floor before entering any multi-unit negotiation
anti_rework_rules.prevents: ad-hoc concessions that spread through the book as every fleet demands the price its neighbor improvised

iteration_protocol.trigger: the platform vendor changes fees, shares, data pricing, or agreement terms
iteration_protocol.action: re-run the per-unit model, recheck the floor under the published ladder, and revisit the channel decision if the change is structural

iteration_protocol.trigger: a pilot completes with measured lines
iteration_protocol.action: replace the account's estimated ROI ranges with observed data and fold the learning into the segment's case template

iteration_protocol.trigger: deals die repeatedly at the same gate condition or segment win rates collapse
iteration_protocol.action: trace the failing condition upstream and re-rank the segment map and beachhead choice

iteration_protocol.trigger: a jurisdiction changes ELD/HOS, telematics-privacy, or employee-monitoring rules
iteration_protocol.action: re-verify the obligation-class map and purge or update every sales script and quote clause that touches the changed class

iteration_protocol.trigger: a competitor restructures pricing or adds local install capability in the market
iteration_protocol.action: revisit the wedge story and offer packaging without touching the cost-stack floor

iteration_protocol.trigger: distributor hardware pricing, warranty terms, or availability shift
iteration_protocol.action: re-source or re-quote landed cost, re-run subsidy recovery math, and adjust the hardware posture rules

iteration_protocol.trigger: a pre-registered channel graduation threshold is crossed
iteration_protocol.action: re-run the channel decision on current evidence, including the two-structure switching cost
